He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==Early life and high school career== Dosunmu was born in [[Chicago]] to Nigerian immigrants. He descends from the [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]] people in Nigeria and his nickname “Ayo” means joy in Yoruba language. Dosunmu began his high school career at Chicago's Westinghouse College Prep, where he helped lead the Warriors to a 2015 conference championship against Al Raby High School and scored a season-high 40 points against Crane High School as a freshman,https://chicago.suntimes.com/2016/4/8/18490109/michael-o-8217-brien-8217-s-notebook-april-8-2016https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-saturday/2019/5/11/18619086/from-chicago-with-joy-ayo-dosunmu-s-name-and-game-are-fueling-illini-rise earning [[Chicago Sun-Times]] All-City Accolades. Dosunmu transferred after his freshman year to [[Morgan Park High School|Morgan Park]]. During his junior year, Dosunmu led the Mustangs to a 3A State Championship, despite getting hurt in the semi-finals. In his senior year, Dosunmu led the Mustangs once again to a state championship, in which he scored 28 points; breaking an [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] record for points scored in a championship game. In March 2018, Dosunmu was named one of 26 high school seniors who participated in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] on April 8, 2018, at the [[Barclays Center]] in [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City|New York]].{{cite web | url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/mens-basketball/2018-03-08/ayo-play-jordan-brand-classic.html | title=Ayo to play in Jordan Brand Classic | publisher=News-Gazette | date=March 8, 2018 | accessdate=April 4, 2018}} Dosunmu is the third Illini to be selected to play in the Jordan Classic, joining [[Dee Brown (basketball, born 1984)|Dee Brown]] who played for the Red team in 2002 and Jalen Coleman-Lands who played in 2015.{{cite web | url=http://jordanbrandclassic.com/history/ | title=All-Time Jordan Brand All-Americans | publisher=Jordan Brand Classic | date=2018 | accessdate=April 4, 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180405090218/https://jordanbrandclassic.com/history/ | archive-date=April 5, 2018 | url-status=dead }} Dosunmu was also selected to play in the second annual Iverson Roundball Classic All-American Game in April 2018 at [[Souderton Area High School]] outside of [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]].{{cite web | url=http://www.complex.com/sports/2018/03/iverson-classic-roster-announcement | publisher=Complex | title=2nd Annual Iverson Classic to Feature Shareef O'Neal, Mac McClung, and More High School Stars | date=March 21, 2018 | accessdate=April 4, 2018 | author=Yuscavage, Chris}} During his senior season, Dosunmu averaged 25.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, 7.3 assists and 2.7 steals, leading Morgan Park to a second-straight [[Illinois High School Boys Basketball Championship|IHSA Class 3A championship]].{{cite web | url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/daily-southtown/sports/ct-sta-boys-basketball-morgan-park-springfield-southeast-st-0318-20180317-story.html | title=Illinois recruit Ayo Dosunmu leads Morgan Park to second straight Class 3A state title | publisher=Chicago Tribune | date=March 18, 2018 | accessdate=June 4, 2018 | author=Clark, Mike}}{{cite web | url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/2018-05-07/dosunmu-gets-team-usa-camp-invite.html | title=Dosunmu gets Team USA camp invite | publisher=News-Gazette | date=May 7, 2018 | accessdate=June 4, 2018 | author=Richey, Scott}} Dosunmu was also named a Consensus first-team All-State selection by the [[Associated Press]], [[Chicago Tribune]], Chicago Sun-Times, [[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|Champaign-News Gazette]] and Illinois Basketball Coaches Association (IBCA) following his senior season. ===Recruiting=== On October 19, 2017, Dosunmu verbally committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] and head coach [[Brad Underwood]]. Dosunmu announced his commitment to Illinois over [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] at the flagship [[Jordan Brand]] Store on [[State Street (Chicago)|State Street]] in the [[Chicago Loop]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/preps-talk/ayo-dosunmu-commitment-changes-outlook-illinois-basketball | title=Ayo Dosunmu commitment changes the outlook of Illinois basketball | publisher=NBC Sports Chicago | author=Phillips, Scott | date=October 19, 2017 | accessdate=April 4, 2018}} Dosunmu signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] in November 2017 to attend career== [[File:Ayo Dosunmu Trent Frazier.jpg|thumb|upright|Dosunmu (left) with [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] in 2020]] Dosunmu made his college debut on November 8, 2018 against [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville]], recording 18 points on 8-of-15 shooting, with six rebounds, four assists and three steals.{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Ayo Dosunmu lives up to billing in Illinois debut with 18 points in 99-60 rout of Evansville |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-illinois-evansville-ayo-dosunmu-20181108-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=15 November 2018}} Following the season, Dosunmu was named to the All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman Team and was named as an honorable mention for the All-Big 10 Team.{{cite web |title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN |url=https://bigten.org/news/2019/3/11/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx |website=bigten.org |accessdate=4 April 2019 |language=en}} He averaged 13.8 points and 3.3 assists per game as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Ayo Dosunmu's return raises the bar for the Illini. Now they need an NCAA Tournament season. |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-illinois-ayo-dosunmu-returning-20190418-story.html |accessdate=February 12, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=April 18, 2019}} Dosunmu hit a last-second jump shot in a 64–62 win over [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] on January 25, 2020, and finished with 27 points.{{cite news |title=Ayo Dosunmu lifts Illinois over Michigan 64–62 |url=https://wgntv.com/2020/01/25/ayo-dosunmu-lifts-illinois-over-michigan-64-62/ |accessdate=February 12, 2020 |work=WGNTV |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 25, 2020}} On February 11, Dosunmu was injured late in a 70–69 loss to [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]].{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=What's the plan if Ayo Dosunmu can't play the next game? 4 takeaways from Illinois' 70–69 loss to Michigan State. |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-illinois-basketball-michigan-state-ayo-dosunmu-20200212-lzdh2isosndahprf5zmcimclia-story.html |accessdate=February 12, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=February 12, 2020}} Despite an [[Magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]] showing no structural damage, Dosunmu missed the following game against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{cite news |last1=Piper |first1=Derek |title=Dosunmu won't play at Rutgers; Griffin starts for Bezhanishvili |url=https://247sports.com/college/illinois/Article/Illinois-Fighting-Illini-guard-Ayo-Dosunmu-will-not-play-at-Rutgers-Giorgi-Bezhanihvili-Alan-Griffin-143843596/ |accessdate=February 16, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=February 15, 2020}} In his return from injury, Dosunmu scored 24 points in a 62–56 win at [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]].{{cite news |title=Dosunmu scores 24, Illinois beats No. 9 Penn State 62–56 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166232 |accessdate=February 18, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 18, 2020}} At the close of the regular season, Dosunmu was named to the First Team All-Big Ten by the media and Second Team by the coaches.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |accessdate=March 9, 2020}} As a sophomore, Dosunmu averaged 16.6 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 3.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Kissack |first1=Tristen |title=Ayo Dosunmu selected to All-Big Ten First Team |url=https://www.thechampaignroom.com/2020/3/9/21172045/illinois-fighting-illini-basketball-all-big-ten-first-team-ayo-dosunmu |website=The Champaign Room |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=March 25, 2020 |date=March 9, 2020}} Following the season, Dosunmu declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Illinois star Ayo Dosunmu declares for the NBA draft: 'I'm 100% locked in' |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-illinois-basketball-ayo-dosunmu-nba-draft-20200416-oj6w22kugbfvddwooqyy2zsohu-story.html |accessdate=April 16, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=April 15, 2020}} Dosunmu withdrew from the draft to return to Illinois for his junior season on July 31, 2020.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Illinois' Dosunmu says he's returning to chase title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29574345/illinois-ayo-dosunmu-says-plans-withdraw-nba-draft |website=ESPN.com |accessdate=1 August 2020 |language=en |date=1 August 2020}} In his junior season debut on November 25, 2020, Dosunmu recorded 28 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a 122–60 win against [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]].{{cite news |last1=Towery |first1=Terry |title=Dosunmu, Miller lead No. 8 Illinois past NC A&T 122–60 |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/dosunmu-miller-lead-no-8-illinois-past-nc-at-122-60/ |access-date=November 25, 2020 |work=[[Seattle Times]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 25, 2020}} On December 12, he scored a career-high 36 points in an 81–78 loss to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite web |title=Ayo Dosunmu scores 36, but Illini fall 81-78 to Missouri |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/12/12/22172102/ayo-dosunmu-scores-36-illini-fall-81-78-missouri-tigers-illinois-braggin-rights-cockburn-underwood |website=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 6, 2021 |date=December 12, 2020}} On February 6, 2021, he became the third player in program history to register a [[triple-double]], with 21 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists in a 75–60 victory over [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{cite web |last1=Good |first1=Gavin |title=Illini ride Dosunmu's triple-double to win over Wisconsin, game against Michigan postponed |url=https://www.pjstar.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/02/06/illinois-vs-wisconsin-ayo-dosunmu-triple-double-leads-illini-win/4420912001/ |website=[[Journal Star (Peoria)|Journal Star]] |access-date=February 6, 2021 |date=February 6, 2021}} On February 20, Dosunmu recorded his second triple-double, with 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 94–63 win over [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]].{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Ayo Dosunmu triple-double leads Illinois' rout of Minnesota |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-illinois-minnesota-big-ten-ayo-dosunmu-20210220-dfrjn7ul4nbkfinxg4tedf4uv4-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=February 20, 2021 |date=February 20, 2021}} On February 23, Dosunmu suffered a broken nose during a 81–72 loss to [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]].{{cite web |last1=Davis |first=Tyler |title=Michigan State basketball beats No. 4 Illinois, 81-72: Game thread replay |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/michigan-state-basketball-game-vs-105808198.html |website=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=February 23, 2021 |date=February 23, 2021}} On March 14, he recorded 16 points and nine rebounds in a 91–88 win over [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]]. He was named tournament most outstanding player.{{cite web |title=Recap: #2 Illinois Captures Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament Title with 91-88 OT Win Over #5 Ohio State |url=https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/14/mens-basketball-recap-2-illinois-captures-big-ten-tournament-title-with-91-88-ot-win-over-5-ohio-state.aspx |website=[[Big Ten Conference]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 14, 2021}} Dosunmu was a consensus first-team All-American and won the [[Bob Cousy Award]] as top point guard in the nation.{{cite web |title=Bob Cousy Award|url=http://www.hoophallawards.com/cousy.php |access-date=2021-04-06|publisher=[[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] |website=hoophall.com |date=2021}} On April 6, 2021, Dosunmu declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], ending his three-year career with Illinois.{{cite web|url=https://www.bleacherreport.com/articles/10000828-illinois-ayo-dosunmu-declares-for-2021-nba-draft-will-hire-agent|title=Illinois' Ayo Dosunmu Declares for 2021 NBA Draft, Will Hire Agent|website=bleacherreport.com|publisher=Bleacher Report|date=April 6, 2021|accessdate=April 7, 2021}} ==National team career== In May 2018, Dosunmu was among the 32 players who earned an invitation to the training camp at the [[United States Olympic Training Center]] in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]] for USA Basketball Men's U18 National Team in preparation for the [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]]. Dosunmu won a gold medal with the U18 National Team, while averaging 9.5 points, 4.5 assists and 2.3 rebounds during the international competition.{{cite web | url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/2018-06-18/welcome-campus-ayo.html | title=Welcome to campus, Ayo | publisher=News Gazette | date=June 18, 2018 | accessdate=June 20, 2018 |
